name: Linear model
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: The learned object is a weight vector (or matrix) applied affinely to the input features, possibly followed by a fixed link or decision function.
negative_test: Excludes any model with a hidden layer of learned nonlinearities (-> MLP) and any model whose prediction needs stored training points (-> kernel machine).
examples: linear regression; logistic regression; PCA projection; ARIMA coefficients
notes: Root (R6): the affine map is not a modification of another architecture here. Thin by design; MODELS_BRIEF B.1 accepts that a linear model is a real compute profile.

name: Linear regression
positive_test: Affine map with identity output, fitted by least squares or a variant.
negative_test: Not the fitting procedure (OLS, ridge penalty, lasso) -- that is an algorithm.
examples: ols; least squares regression; elastic net (model is the linear one)
notes: Ridge/lasso/elastic-net differ only in the penalty, which is part of the fitting procedure; they are notes on this node, not children.

name: Logistic regression
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: Affine score passed through a logistic link to give a class probability.
negative_test: Not the IRLS/SGD fit, which is an algorithm.
notes: MODELS_BRIEF fixed point: model = linear model with logit link; algorithm = the fitting procedure.

name: Multinomial logistic regression
positive_test: The logistic model extended to more than two classes with a softmax link.
negative_test: Not a softmax output layer inside a deep network, which is a layer of that network.
notes: R1: defined as logistic regression generalised to K classes.

name: Generalized linear model
positive_test: An affine score mapped through a chosen link, with an exponential-family response.
negative_test: Not GAMs or any model with learned nonlinear basis functions.
notes: Lineage, not subsumption: GLM contains linear regression in extension but was DERIVED from it (Nelder & Wedderburn 1972), so it is a child. See RATIONALE reading (b).

name: Perceptron
positive_test: A single linear threshold unit with an online mistake-driven weight update.
negative_test: Not a multi-layer network; `multilayer perceptron' is the MLP root, not this node.
notes: Boundary case: `perceptron' and `multi-layer perceptron' share a word but not an edge in this tree. See BOUNDARY_CASES.

name: Principal component analysis
positive_test: The learned object is an orthogonal projection matrix fitted to maximise retained variance; it applies to unseen inputs.
negative_test: Excludes t-SNE/UMAP/PHATE, which fit an embedding of the training points only and cannot map a new point -- those are algorithms.
examples: pca; kernel pca (-> kernel machine); probabilistic pca
notes: Added in phase 2 (blind spot: a projection/decomposition cluster with no home).

name: Canonical correlation analysis
positive_test: Two learned linear projections, one per view, maximising cross-view correlation.
negative_test: Not deep CCA, which is a pair of MLPs (-> MLP).
notes: Added in phase 2.

name: Linear discriminant analysis
positive_test: A learned linear projection plus per-class Gaussian decision rule.
negative_test: Not latent Dirichlet allocation, which shares the acronym `lda' and is a directed graphical model.
notes: Added in phase 2. The `lda' acronym collides with latent Dirichlet allocation; SPELLINGS refuses to resolve the bare acronym.

name: Cox proportional hazards model
positive_test: A linear predictor of log-hazard with an unspecified baseline hazard.
negative_test: Not the partial-likelihood fitting procedure.
examples: cox model; cox regression; deepsurv (-> MLP)
notes: Added in phase 2; semi-parametric, kept here because the learned object is the coefficient vector.

name: ARIMA
positive_test: Linear in lagged observations and past innovations; parameters are the AR/MA coefficients.
negative_test: Not a state space model: ARIMA has a state-space form but was not derived from one.
notes: Boundary case: placed by framing (Box-Jenkins), not by the equivalence with a linear-Gaussian SSM.

name: Kernel machine
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: Prediction is a learned weighted sum of kernel evaluations between the input and stored training points; the learned object is the coefficients plus the retained points and kernel hyperparameters.
negative_test: Excludes k-NN and kernel density estimation: nothing is learned, so there is no separable learned object (MODELS_BRIEF B.1).
examples: svm; gaussian process; kernel ridge regression
notes: Root (R6). Lineage, not subsumption: a linear SVM is also a linear model, and both edges are kept (DAG, 3.1).

name: Support vector machine
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A max-margin decision function expressed over support vectors.
negative_test: Not the SMO/QP solver, which is an algorithm.

name: Linear SVM
positive_test: An SVM with a linear kernel.
notes: Also describable as a linear model; the second edge is not asserted because the framing is SVM-first.

name: Support vector regression
positive_test: An SVM with an epsilon-insensitive loss for regression.

name: One-class SVM
positive_test: An SVM fitted to a single class for novelty detection.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Gaussian process
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A prior over functions with a learned covariance kernel; prediction conditions on the stored training set.
negative_test: Not Bayesian optimisation, which is an acquisition procedure using a GP (-> algorithms).
examples: gaussian process; gp regression; gp classifier
notes: Boundary case: the learned object is the kernel hyperparameters plus retained data. Admitted because hyperparameters are learned; k-NN is excluded because nothing is.

name: Deep Gaussian process
positive_test: A composition of GP layers.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Neural process
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: An encoder aggregating a permutation-invariant context set into a representation that conditions a decoder, giving a learned stochastic process.
negative_test: Not a Gaussian process: the predictive distribution is amortised by networks, not computed in closed form.
examples: cnp; np; anp; constant memory attentive neural processes
notes: Added in phase 2 (blind spot). Two parents: the DeepSets-style permutation-invariant aggregation (R1, cited in the CNP paper) and the GP the family amortises. The GP edge is the weaker of the two -- see BOUNDARY_CASES.

name: Transformer neural process
positive_test: A neural process whose context aggregation is self-attention rather than mean pooling.
examples: tnp; eqtnp; latent bottlenecked attentive neural processes
notes: Added in phase 2. R5 hybrid.

name: Kernel ridge regression
positive_test: Ridge regression in a kernel feature space.

name: Decision tree
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A recursive partition of the input space; the learned object is the split variables, thresholds and leaf values.
negative_test: Not the induction procedure (CART's growth, pruning, surrogate splits) and not a rule list learned directly as rules (-> rule-based model).
examples: decision tree; classification tree; regression tree
notes: Root (R6). Overlaps `Rule-based model' in extension; neither derives from the other, so both are roots (1.3).

name: CART
positive_test: The CART tree: binary axis-aligned splits with Gini/variance criteria.

name: ID3
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: Quinlan's information-gain tree over categorical attributes.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2); kept as the head of a real lineage.

name: C4.5
positive_test: ID3 extended with continuous attributes, pruning and missing values.
notes: R1: framed by its author as the successor to ID3.

name: Decision stump
positive_test: A depth-one tree.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Tree ensemble
characteristic: how the member trees enter the prediction: averaged over independently grown trees, or summed over sequentially fitted ones
positive_test: A predictor that aggregates many decision trees into one output.
negative_test: Not a single tree, and not an ensemble of non-tree learners (that is a run-level fact, not a model).
examples: random forest; gradient boosted trees; xgboost
notes: Descent from `Decision tree' (it cannot be described without naming trees); it divides its own children.

name: Bagged tree ensemble
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: The member trees are grown independently on resampled data/features and their outputs are averaged or voted.
negative_test: Excludes any ensemble whose members are fitted to the previous members' residuals.
examples: random forest; extremely randomized trees; isolation forest
notes: R4: the field names bagging; two substantive children; definable without listing them.

name: Random forest
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: Bagged trees with a random feature subset considered at each split.
negative_test: Not the bagging + random-subspace procedure, which is an algorithm.
examples: random forest; random forest classifier; generalized random forests
notes: MODELS_BRIEF fixed point: model = decision-tree ensemble; algorithm = bagging + random subspace.

name: Extremely randomized trees
positive_test: A random forest whose split thresholds are also drawn at random.
notes: R1: framed against random forests. Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Isolation forest
positive_test: Random trees whose path length scores anomaly.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Boosted tree ensemble
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: The member trees are fitted sequentially to the current residual/gradient and summed with shrinkage.
negative_test: Excludes independently grown, averaged ensembles.
notes: R4: the field names boosting; two substantive children; definable without listing them.

name: Gradient-boosted decision trees
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: An additive tree ensemble fitted to the gradient of a differentiable loss.
negative_test: Not the boosting procedure itself (-> algorithms).
examples: gbm; gradient boosting machine; gradient boosted trees
notes: MODELS_BRIEF fixed point via XGBoost.

name: XGBoost
positive_test: The XGBoost release: regularised objective, sparsity-aware split finding.
notes: R3: a separately named release. Also a library name; the library sense belongs in libraries[].

name: LightGBM
positive_test: Histogram-based, leaf-wise-grown GBDT.

name: CatBoost
positive_test: Ordered boosting with native categorical handling.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: AdaBoost ensemble
positive_test: The weighted ensemble of weak learners produced by AdaBoost.
negative_test: Not the AdaBoost reweighting procedure, which is an algorithm.
notes: Boundary case: AdaBoost is base-learner-agnostic; it sits here because its canonical base learner is a stump.

name: Feedforward network (MLP)
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A stack of dense affine layers with elementwise nonlinearities: no weight sharing across positions, no state carried across steps, no input-supplied graph.
negative_test: Excludes convolutional, recurrent, attentional and message-passing stacks; excludes a bare `neural network' string, which is quarantined.
examples: mlp; multilayer perceptron; fully connected network; feed-forward neural network
notes: Root (R6). Boundary case: considered as a child of `Perceptron'/`Linear model' and rejected -- the connectionist framing is not `a modified linear regression', and the edge would make almost every network a linear-model descendant, destroying that cut.

name: MLP-Mixer
positive_test: Token-mixing and channel-mixing MLPs over image patches.
notes: R1: `an architecture based exclusively on multi-layer perceptrons'.

name: Deep Sets
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A per-element MLP followed by a permutation-invariant pooling and a second MLP.
negative_test: Excludes any model whose output depends on input order.

name: PointNet
positive_test: Per-point MLP with symmetric max pooling over an unordered point set.
negative_test: Not a 3-D convnet over a voxel grid (-> CNN).
notes: Boundary case: contemporaneous with Deep Sets rather than derived from it; the edge is on the shared permutation-invariant construction, which is close to an R2 similarity edge.

name: Bayesian neural network
positive_test: A network whose weights are random variables with learned posterior parameters, so `parameter_count' counts distribution parameters.
negative_test: Not a deep ensemble (N copies of one architecture: the model is that architecture, the count is a run property) and not MC-dropout at test time.
examples: bayesian neural network; bnn; bayesian nested neural network; bayesian u-net (-> U-Net too)
notes: Added in phase 2 (blind spot). Boundary case: `Bayesian' is a cross-cutting parameterisation that can apply to any architecture; the MLP parent is the canonical instantiation only.

name: Coordinate MLP (implicit neural representation)
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: An MLP that maps continuous input coordinates to a field value, so the signal is stored in the weights rather than in a grid.
negative_test: Excludes grid- or primitive-based representations with no network (-> 3D Gaussian splatting).
notes: R4: the field names implicit neural representations; four substantive children; definable without listing them.

name: NeRF
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A coordinate MLP mapping position and view direction to colour and density, rendered by volume integration.

name: Instant-NGP
positive_test: NeRF with a multiresolution hash encoding.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Mip-NeRF
positive_test: NeRF with conical-frustum (anti-aliased) sampling.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: SIREN
positive_test: A coordinate MLP with sinusoidal activations.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: DeepSDF
positive_test: A coordinate MLP regressing a signed distance field.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Occupancy network
positive_test: A coordinate MLP predicting occupancy probability.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Convolutional network
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: Learned filters applied by weight-shared local correlation over a grid-structured input; layers are translation-equivariant by construction.
negative_test: Excludes message passing over an input-supplied graph (-> GNN) and attention over a token set (-> Transformer). A `cnn' string with no further specification resolves here, not to a release.
notes: Root (R6).

name: LeNet
positive_test: The LeNet-5 convnet.

name: AlexNet
positive_test: The 2012 ImageNet convnet with ReLU and dropout.

name: VGG
positive_test: A deep stack of 3x3 convolutions in uniform blocks.
notes: Size/depth variants (vgg-11/16/19) are separate nodes by R3, grown by the second pass.

name: Inception (GoogLeNet)
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A convnet of parallel multi-scale branches concatenated per block.

name: Xception
positive_test: Inception taken to the limit with depthwise separable convolutions.
notes: R1: `Extreme Inception'.

name: ResNet
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A convnet whose blocks add an identity shortcut around the learned residual.
negative_test: Not any network that merely has skip connections (U-Net's skips concatenate across the resolution path).
notes: MODELS_BRIEF worked case: `a CNN with residual connections'. Depth variants are nodes by R3, grown by the second pass.

name: ResNeXt
positive_test: ResNet with grouped (cardinality) convolutions.

name: Wide ResNet
positive_test: ResNet widened rather than deepened.

name: SE-ResNet (SENet)
positive_test: ResNet blocks with squeeze-and-excitation channel recalibration.

name: ConvNeXt
positive_test: A ResNet modernised with large kernels, LayerNorm and an inverted bottleneck.
notes: R1: `we gradually modernize a standard ResNet'. The influence of Swin is R2, not an edge.

name: Neural ODE
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A network whose forward pass is the solution of a learned ODE: the continuous-depth limit of a residual stack.
negative_test: Not a neural operator (which maps between function spaces).
examples: neural ode; ode-net; augmented neural ode
notes: R1: framed as the limit of residual networks.

name: DenseNet
positive_test: A convnet concatenating every earlier feature map into each layer's input.
notes: Boundary case: the paper names ResNet heavily, but to contrast connectivity patterns, not to derive from it (reading (d)). Parent is CNN.

name: MobileNet
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A convnet built from depthwise separable convolutions for low compute.

name: EfficientNet
positive_test: Compound-scaled inverted-bottleneck convnet.
notes: Boundary case: derived from the MobileNetV2/MnasNet block family; the contribution is the scaling rule, which is arguably a procedure.

name: ShuffleNet
positive_test: Grouped convolutions with channel shuffling.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: SqueezeNet
positive_test: Fire modules squeezing channel count for parameter economy.

name: Time-delay neural network
positive_test: A 1-D convnet over a temporal context window, weight-shared across time.
negative_test: Not a recurrent network: there is no carried state.
notes: Added in phase 2 (speech cluster had no named home).

name: R-CNN
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A convnet classifier applied to region proposals for detection.
notes: Series head: Fast/Faster/Mask R-CNN attach here by the series-flattening rule, with their predecessor in notes.

name: Fast R-CNN
positive_test: R-CNN with RoI pooling over a shared feature map.
notes: Predecessor: R-CNN.

name: Faster R-CNN
positive_test: Fast R-CNN with a learned region proposal network.
notes: Predecessor: Fast R-CNN.

name: Mask R-CNN
positive_test: Faster R-CNN with a parallel mask branch.
notes: Predecessor: Faster R-CNN.

name: YOLO
positive_test: A single-stage convnet predicting boxes and classes on one grid pass.
notes: Boundary case: the paper names R-CNN to contrast, not to derive (reading (d)). Generations attach here.

name: SSD
positive_test: Single-shot multibox detection from multiple feature scales.

name: RetinaNet
positive_test: One-stage detector with a feature pyramid.

name: Feature pyramid network
positive_test: A top-down pathway with lateral connections building a multi-scale feature pyramid.
notes: Possibly speculative as a standalone model: it is usually a component. Kept because it is separately named and separately run.

name: Encoder-decoder convnet
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A convnet whose spatial resolution is reduced and then restored by learned upsampling, producing an output on the input grid.
negative_test: Excludes classification backbones that end in a pooled vector; excludes dilated-convolution models that never downsample.
notes: R4: the field names fully-convolutional encoder-decoders; three substantive children; definable without listing them. Chosen as structural, not task-based: U-Net denoises latents inside Stable Diffusion, where no segmentation occurs.

name: Fully convolutional network
positive_test: A classification convnet converted to dense prediction with learned upsampling.

name: U-Net
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A symmetric encoder-decoder convnet with skip connections concatenating encoder features into the matching decoder stage.
examples: u-net; unet; v-net; transunet (-> Transformer too)
notes: MODELS_BRIEF worked case. Heavily reused outside segmentation: it is the usual denoiser inside diffusion systems.

name: 3D U-Net
positive_test: U-Net with volumetric convolutions.

name: nnU-Net
positive_test: A self-configuring U-Net pipeline.
notes: Boundary case: largely a configuration procedure around a U-Net; kept as a node because it is named and run as a model.

name: Attention U-Net
positive_test: U-Net with attention gates on the skip connections.

name: SegNet
positive_test: Encoder-decoder convnet upsampling with stored pooling indices.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: DeepLab
positive_test: Dilated (atrous) convolutions with spatial pyramid pooling for dense prediction.
notes: Not under the encoder-decoder node: v1/v2 never restore resolution by learned upsampling.

name: WaveNet
positive_test: Stacked dilated causal convolutions over raw audio.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Temporal convolutional network
positive_test: Dilated causal 1-D convolutions for sequence modelling.

name: PixelCNN
positive_test: Masked convolutions giving an autoregressive factorisation over pixels.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: I3D
positive_test: A 2-D convnet inflated to 3-D for video.
notes: R1: `inflated' from an ImageNet convnet.

name: SlowFast
positive_test: Two-pathway video convnet at different frame rates.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Group-equivariant CNN
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A convnet whose weight sharing is over a larger symmetry group than translation.
negative_test: Excludes equivariance obtained by data augmentation.
examples: g-cnn; p4-cnn; frame averaging networks; canonicalization networks
notes: R1: framed as generalising the CNN's translation equivariance.

name: Steerable CNN
positive_test: Group-equivariant convnet with steerable filter bases over continuous groups.
notes: Possibly speculative under this exact name (phase 2); the equivariance cluster itself is well attested.

name: Capsule network
positive_test: Vector-valued capsules with routing by agreement replacing pooling.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Recurrent network
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A hidden state carried from one sequence position to the next by a weight-shared transition.
negative_test: Excludes attention-only models and excludes convolutional sequence models with a fixed receptive field.
notes: Root (R6). The Transformer is NOT a child: it is framed as dispensing with recurrence (reading (d)).

name: Elman RNN
positive_test: The simple recurrent network with a tanh state update.
examples: elman network; vanilla rnn; simple rnn; 2rnn

name: LSTM
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A recurrent cell with a gated memory cell and input/forget/output gates.

name: BiLSTM
positive_test: Two LSTMs run in opposite directions over the sequence.

name: ConvLSTM
positive_test: An LSTM whose gate transforms are convolutions over a spatial grid.
notes: R5 hybrid.

name: Tree-LSTM
positive_test: An LSTM composed over a tree structure instead of a chain.

name: GRU
positive_test: A recurrent cell with reset and update gates and no separate memory cell.
notes: Boundary case: framed as `motivated by the LSTM unit but simpler'. That is R2 influence, so the LSTM edge is NOT asserted.

name: Echo state network
positive_test: A fixed random recurrent reservoir with only the readout trained.
examples: echo state network; esn; reservoir computing

name: Neural Turing Machine
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A recurrent controller with an addressable external memory read and written by differentiable attention.
notes: Possibly speculative under this name (phase 2); its successor is attested.

name: Differentiable Neural Computer
positive_test: NTM with improved memory allocation and temporal linking.

name: Memory network
positive_test: A network with an explicit memory array queried by a controller.

name: Seq2seq
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: An encoder RNN compressing a sequence into a vector that a decoder RNN expands.
notes: R1: `a multilayered LSTM maps the input to a fixed vector and another deep LSTM decodes'.

name: Attentional seq2seq
positive_test: Seq2seq whose decoder attends over all encoder states.
examples: bahdanau attention model; luong attention model
notes: Historically the parent of attention, but NOT of the Transformer, which is framed as a replacement (reading (d)).

name: PixelRNN
positive_test: Row/diagonal LSTMs factorising an image autoregressively.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: RWKV
positive_test: A linear-attention formulation trainable in parallel like a Transformer and runnable as an RNN.
notes: R5 hybrid. Attached to the decoder-only division, not to `transformer` directly: a direct child would sit beside the three division nodes and break their totality (self-audit repair). Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Transformer
characteristic: which of the original architecture's two stacks the model retains, and hence the attention mask: bidirectional over the whole input, causal over its own output, or both joined by cross-attention
positive_test: Stacked self-attention over a set of tokens with positional information, with no recurrence and no convolution in the backbone.
negative_test: Excludes attention added to a recurrent or convolutional backbone (-> that backbone), and excludes a bare `attention-based model' string, which is quarantined.
notes: Root (R6); MODELS_BRIEF worked case. The division is total: every descendant falls under exactly one of the three stacks.

name: Encoder-only Transformer
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: Keeps the encoder stack only: every token attends to every other, and there is no causal mask.
negative_test: Excludes models that generate token by token under a causal mask.
notes: R4: universal field usage; many substantive children; definable without listing them.

name: Decoder-only Transformer
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: Keeps the decoder stack only: causal self-attention over the model's own output, no cross-attention.
negative_test: Excludes bidirectional encoders and excludes two-stack translation models.
notes: R4, same principle as its siblings.

name: Encoder-decoder Transformer
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: Keeps both stacks: a bidirectional encoder and a causal decoder joined by cross-attention.
negative_test: Excludes single-stack models; a prefix-LM is a boundary case recorded separately.
notes: R4, same principle as its siblings.

name: BERT
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: The BERT release: a bidirectional Transformer encoder pretrained with masked-language modelling.
negative_test: Not any bidirectional encoder: a model is a BERT descendant only if its own framing names BERT.
notes: MODELS_BRIEF worked case. Flagged in SELF_AUDIT for a deeper design pass: its variant set is wide and heterogeneous.

name: RoBERTa
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: BERT with longer, larger, dynamically masked pretraining and no NSP.
notes: R1: `a robustly optimized BERT pretraining approach'. Differs from parent by: pretraining recipe.

name: XLM-R
positive_test: RoBERTa's objective trained on 100-language CommonCrawl.
notes: Differs from parent by: pretraining corpus and language coverage.

name: ALBERT
positive_test: BERT with factorised embeddings and cross-layer parameter sharing.
notes: Differs from parent by: parameter sharing (architecture).

name: DistilBERT
positive_test: A distilled, halved-depth BERT.
notes: MODELS_BRIEF worked case. Differs from parent by: capacity and training objective (distillation).

name: ELECTRA
positive_test: BERT-style encoder pretrained as a replaced-token discriminator.
notes: Differs from parent by: pretraining objective.

name: DeBERTa
positive_test: BERT with disentangled content/position attention and an enhanced decoder head.
notes: Differs from parent by: attention architecture and objective -- an example of why the BERT-variant division does not partition.

name: TinyBERT
positive_test: A small BERT distilled at several layers.
notes: Differs from parent by: capacity.

name: MobileBERT
positive_test: A bottlenecked, thin-deep BERT for on-device use.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Sentence-BERT
positive_test: A siamese-tuned BERT producing sentence embeddings.
notes: Differs from parent by: training objective and pooling head.

name: Multilingual BERT
positive_test: BERT pretrained on 104 Wikipedias jointly.
notes: Differs from parent by: pretraining corpus.

name: BioBERT
positive_test: BERT further pretrained on biomedical text.
notes: Differs from parent by: pretraining corpus. Possibly speculative under this exact name (phase 2): the domain-variant PATTERN is large in the corpus but populated by different instances.

name: SciBERT
positive_test: BERT pretrained on scientific text with its own vocabulary.
notes: Differs from parent by: pretraining corpus and vocabulary. Possibly speculative under this exact name (phase 2).

name: ClinicalBERT
positive_test: BERT further pretrained on clinical notes.
notes: Differs from parent by: pretraining corpus. Possibly speculative under this exact name (phase 2).

name: CodeBERT
positive_test: BERT pretrained on paired code and natural language.
notes: MODELS_BRIEF worked case. Differs from parent by: pretraining data.

name: ProtBERT
positive_test: BERT pretrained on protein sequences.
notes: Differs from parent by: pretraining corpus.

name: Vision Transformer (ViT)
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A Transformer encoder over a sequence of flattened image patches with a learned patch embedding.
negative_test: Not a convnet with an attention block (-> CNN).
notes: MODELS_BRIEF worked case, with one deviation recorded in BOUNDARY_CASES: the brief places ViT directly under `transformer', this tree places it under the encoder-only division so that the division stays total.

name: DeiT
positive_test: A ViT trained data-efficiently with a distillation token.

name: Swin Transformer
positive_test: A hierarchical ViT with shifted local attention windows.

name: BEiT
positive_test: A ViT pretrained with BERT-style masked image-token prediction.
notes: R5 hybrid: the title names both parents.

name: Masked autoencoder (MAE)
positive_test: An asymmetric ViT encoder-decoder trained to reconstruct masked patches.
notes: R5 hybrid.

name: DINOv2
positive_test: The released self-distilled ViT backbone.
negative_test: Not the DINO training objective, which is an algorithm.
notes: The `dino' string is ambiguous between the objective (algorithm) and the released backbone; SPELLINGS refuses to resolve it.

name: Segment Anything (SAM)
positive_test: A ViT image encoder with a prompt encoder and a lightweight mask decoder.
notes: Composite in shape but named and released as one model. The `sam' string also collides with the SAM optimiser (an algorithm).

name: Diffusion Transformer (DiT)
positive_test: A ViT operating on latent patches as the denoiser of a diffusion system.
notes: R1 to ViT; the U-Net it replaces is a contrast, not a parent (reading (d)).

name: wav2vec 2.0
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A convolutional feature encoder feeding a Transformer encoder, pretrained by contrastive masked prediction over quantised units.
notes: R5 hybrid.

name: HuBERT
positive_test: wav2vec 2.0's architecture pretrained to predict offline-clustered units.
notes: Differs from parent by: pretraining target.

name: Conformer
positive_test: A Transformer encoder block with a convolution module inserted.
notes: MODELS_BRIEF worked case for R5 hybrid.

name: Perceiver
positive_test: Cross-attention from a large input array into a small latent array refined by self-attention.

name: ESM
positive_test: A Transformer encoder protein language model over amino-acid sequences.

name: AlphaFold
positive_test: A composite protein-structure model: an attention stack over an MSA/pair representation feeding an equivariant structure module.
negative_test: Not the MSA search pipeline around it.
notes: Added in phase 2 (blind spot). Composite in shape; the structure module is equivariant rather than a plain encoder.

name: GPT
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: The GPT line: a causal Transformer decoder pretrained on next-token prediction.
negative_test: Not any decoder-only LM: the framing must name GPT.
notes: Series head. Generations attach here by the series-flattening rule, with the predecessor in notes.

name: GPT-2
positive_test: The GPT-2 release.
notes: Predecessor: GPT.

name: GPT-3
positive_test: The GPT-3 release.
notes: Predecessor: GPT-2 (`same model and architecture as GPT-2').

name: GPT-3.5
positive_test: The GPT-3.5 release family.
notes: Predecessor: GPT-3, instruction-tuned.

name: GPT-4
positive_test: The GPT-4 release family.
notes: Predecessor: GPT-3.5 by generation; the technical report asserts no architecture, so the edge rests on the series name.

name: ChatGPT
positive_test: The deployed chat product whose served model is a GPT-3.5 or GPT-4 release.
negative_test: Not a distinct architecture; it is a product surface over a GPT release.
notes: Added in phase 2. Boundary case: product names vs model releases.

name: Codex
positive_test: A GPT model fine-tuned on public code.
notes: Added in phase 2. R1: `a GPT language model fine-tuned on publicly available code'. Copilot is the product over it.

name: GPT-NeoX
positive_test: Open replications of the GPT-3 architecture.
notes: Differs from parent by: open weights and training corpus.

name: LLaMA
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: The LLaMA line: a causal decoder with pre-norm, SwiGLU and rotary embeddings, trained on public data.
notes: Series head.

name: Llama 2
positive_test: The Llama 2 release family.
notes: Predecessor: LLaMA. Size variants are separate nodes by R3, grown by the second pass.

name: Llama 3
positive_test: The Llama 3 release family.
notes: Predecessor: Llama 2.

name: Vicuna
positive_test: LLaMA instruction-tuned on shared conversations.
notes: MODELS_BRIEF worked case. Differs from parent by: fine-tuning data.

name: Alpaca
positive_test: LLaMA instruction-tuned on self-instruct data.
notes: Differs from parent by: fine-tuning data.

name: Code Llama
positive_test: Llama 2 further trained on code.
notes: Predecessor: Llama 2.

name: Mistral
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: The Mistral line: a decoder with sliding-window and grouped-query attention.

name: Mixtral
positive_test: Mistral with sparse mixture-of-experts feed-forward blocks.
notes: Mixture-of-experts is recorded here as a property, not as a node: it is a layer-level fact (BOUNDARY_CASES).

name: OPT
positive_test: The OPT open decoder family.

name: BLOOM
positive_test: The BLOOM multilingual open decoder.

name: Falcon
positive_test: The Falcon open decoder family.

name: PaLM
positive_test: The PaLM decoder family.

name: Gopher
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: The Gopher decoder family.

name: Chinchilla
positive_test: A compute-optimal retraining of the Gopher architecture.
notes: Differs from parent by: parameter/token budget. Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Qwen
positive_test: The Qwen decoder family.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Gemma
positive_test: The Gemma open decoder family.

name: Phi
positive_test: The Phi small decoder family trained on curated data.

name: DeepSeek
positive_test: The DeepSeek decoder family.

name: OLMo
positive_test: The fully open OLMo decoder family.

name: Claude
positive_test: The Claude released model family.
notes: Closed weights; attached on the vendor's own description as a Transformer LM.

name: Gemini
positive_test: The Gemini released multimodal model family.
examples: gemini; gemini pro; gemini 1.5 pro; gemini nano; bard
notes: Closed weights. `Bard' is the product surface.

name: Transformer-XL
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A decoder with segment-level recurrence and relative positions.

name: XLNet
positive_test: Permutation language modelling on the Transformer-XL backbone.
notes: Boundary case: framed against BERT as well; only the architectural parent is asserted.

name: Decision Transformer
positive_test: A causal Transformer over (return, state, action) tokens.
negative_test: Not the offline RL algorithm it replaces.

name: T5
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A text-to-text encoder-decoder pretrained with span corruption.

name: mT5
positive_test: T5 pretrained multilingually.
notes: Differs from parent by: pretraining corpus.

name: Flan-T5
positive_test: T5 instruction-tuned on the Flan mixture.
notes: Differs from parent by: fine-tuning data.

name: ByT5
positive_test: T5 operating on raw bytes.
notes: Differs from parent by: tokenisation.

name: UL2
positive_test: A T5-style model with a mixture-of-denoisers objective and mode switching.
notes: Boundary case: a prefix-LM, so the encoder/decoder division is strained. Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: BART
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A denoising encoder-decoder pretrained to reconstruct corrupted text.

name: mBART
positive_test: BART pretrained multilingually.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Pegasus
positive_test: An encoder-decoder pretrained with gap-sentence generation.

name: Whisper
positive_test: An encoder-decoder over log-mel frames for speech recognition and translation.

name: DETR
positive_test: A convolutional backbone feeding a Transformer encoder-decoder that predicts a set of boxes.
notes: R5 hybrid.

name: CLIP
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: Two encoders, one per modality, trained to a shared embedding space.
negative_test: Not the contrastive objective, which is an algorithm.
notes: MODELS_BRIEF worked case for R5 composite. Released ResNet-image-encoder variants additionally descend from ResNet.

name: BLIP
positive_test: A ViT image encoder with a text encoder-decoder and cross-attention.
notes: R5 composite.

name: Flamingo
positive_test: A frozen vision encoder bridged by gated cross-attention into a frozen LM.
notes: R5 composite.

name: LLaVA
positive_test: A CLIP vision encoder projected into a LLaMA decoder.
notes: R5 composite; both parents are themselves composites.

name: Stable Diffusion
positive_test: A latent diffusion system: a VAE for the latent space, a U-Net denoiser, a CLIP text encoder.
negative_test: Not the diffusion procedure, which is an algorithm.
examples: stable diffusion; stable diffusion 2.1; sdxl; latent diffusion
notes: R5 composite, and the template for every named diffusion system.

name: Imagen
positive_test: A frozen T5 text encoder conditioning a cascade of diffusion U-Nets.
notes: Added in phase 2. R5 composite.

name: DALL-E 2
positive_test: A CLIP-latent prior with a diffusion decoder.
notes: Added in phase 2. R5 composite.

name: Graph neural network
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: Permutation-equivariant message passing over a graph supplied with the input; the learned object is the message/update functions.
negative_test: Excludes attention over a fully connected token set with no input graph (-> Transformer) and excludes graph *embeddings*, where the learned object is a vector table (-> embedding model).
notes: Root (R6). Boundary case: spectral GNNs are framed as generalising convolution to graphs, but that is the primitive, and R2 forbids a primitive edge.

name: ChebNet
positive_test: Spectral graph convolution with a Chebyshev polynomial filter.
notes: Possibly speculative under this name (phase 2).

name: GCN
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: Symmetric-normalised neighbourhood averaging with a shared linear map per layer.
examples: gcn; graph convolutional network; gcnii; gatedgcn

name: R-GCN
positive_test: A GCN with relation-specific weight matrices.
notes: Possibly speculative under this name (phase 2).

name: GAT
positive_test: Attention-weighted neighbourhood aggregation.
examples: gat; graph attention network; gatv2; han

name: GraphSAGE
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: Sampled-neighbourhood aggregation designed for inductive use.

name: PinSAGE
positive_test: GraphSAGE scaled with random-walk sampling for web-scale recommendation.

name: GIN
positive_test: Sum aggregation with an MLP, matched to the WL test's power.

name: Message passing neural network
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: The message-passing formulation with edge-conditioned messages and a readout.
notes: Boundary case: also a *framework* that subsumes GCN/GAT in extension; the edge is lineage, not subsumption.

name: SchNet
positive_test: Continuous-filter convolutions over interatomic distances.

name: DimeNet
positive_test: Directional message passing with angular basis functions.

name: E(n)-equivariant GNN
positive_test: Message passing equivariant to rotation, translation and reflection of coordinates.
examples: egnn; e(n)-equivariant gnn; clofnet; equibind; gvp

name: Graph Transformer
positive_test: Self-attention over nodes with structural/positional encodings standing in for the adjacency.
notes: R5 hybrid.

name: Graph autoencoder
positive_test: A GNN encoder with an inner-product or decoder reconstructing the graph.
notes: R5 hybrid.

name: Probabilistic graphical model
characteristic: the edge semantics of the factorization: directed conditional factors, or undirected potentials over cliques
positive_test: The learned object is a set of factors over variables whose dependency structure is a graph.
negative_test: Excludes a neural network that merely outputs a distribution; the graph must be over the modelled variables.
examples: bayesian network; hmm; crf; boltzmann machine
notes: Root (R6).

name: Directed graphical model (Bayesian network)
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: Factors are conditional distributions of a variable given its parents in a DAG.
negative_test: Excludes undirected potentials.
examples: bayesian network; naive bayes; hmm; lda
notes: R4: the field names Bayesian networks; four substantive children; definable without listing them.

name: Naive Bayes
positive_test: Class-conditional independence of all features.
examples: naive bayes; bayes classifier; multinomial nb

name: Hidden Markov model
positive_test: A discrete latent state with Markov transitions and per-state emissions.
negative_test: Not the Baum-Welch/Viterbi procedures.
examples: hmm; hidden markov model; markov switching model
notes: Two parents: a dynamic Bayesian network and a discrete-state state space model.

name: Latent Dirichlet allocation
positive_test: Documents as Dirichlet mixtures over word-topic distributions.
negative_test: Not linear discriminant analysis, which shares the `lda' acronym.
notes: Possibly speculative under this name (phase 2); the acronym collision is recorded in SPELLINGS and BOUNDARY_CASES.

name: Mixture model
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A latent discrete component index with per-component densities.
negative_test: Not k-means, where nothing probabilistic is learned.

name: Gaussian mixture model
positive_test: Mixture of Gaussians with learned weights, means and covariances.
notes: Possibly speculative under this name (phase 2).

name: Bayesian hierarchical model
positive_test: A multi-level directed model with hyperpriors shared across groups.
negative_test: Not any model merely fitted by Bayesian inference.
examples: bayesian hierarchical model; bhm; multilevel model
notes: Added in phase 2: a cluster of applied statistical models with no home.

name: Undirected graphical model (Markov random field)
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: Factors are non-negative potentials over cliques of an undirected graph, normalised globally.
negative_test: Excludes directed conditional factorisations.
examples: crf; ising model; boltzmann machine; hopfield network
notes: R4: the field names Markov random fields; four substantive children; definable without listing them.

name: Conditional random field
positive_test: An MRF over labels conditioned on the whole input.

name: Markov random field (Ising/Potts)
positive_test: Pairwise potentials over a lattice or general graph.
notes: Possibly speculative under this name (phase 2).

name: Hopfield network
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: Symmetric recurrent weights with an energy function and attractor dynamics for associative recall.
notes: Phase-1 decision: no separate `energy-based' root; energy is a property, not a lineage.

name: Modern Hopfield network
positive_test: A continuous Hopfield network with exponential capacity and an attention-like update.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Boltzmann machine
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A stochastic undirected network with hidden units and an energy function.
notes: R1: a stochastic generalisation of the Hopfield network; the undirected-GM parent is the structural one.

name: Restricted Boltzmann machine
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A Boltzmann machine with no intra-layer connections.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Deep belief network
positive_test: A stack of RBMs with a directed lower part.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Deep Boltzmann machine
positive_test: A Boltzmann machine with several hidden layers, all undirected.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: State space model
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A latent state evolving under a transition operator and read out by an emission operator; the learned object is those operators.
negative_test: Excludes a recurrent cell with a learned nonlinear gate (-> RNN) unless the paper frames it as a state space model.
notes: Root (R6). Spans the classical linear-Gaussian models and the deep sequence models that explicitly derive from them.

name: Linear dynamical system (Kalman filter model)
positive_test: Linear-Gaussian transition and emission.
negative_test: Not the Kalman filter recursion, which is the inference algorithm.
examples: linear dynamical system; kalman filter model; garch-ssm
notes: Possibly speculative under this name (phase 2).

name: S4
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A structured state space sequence model with HiPPO initialisation, computable as a long convolution or a recurrence.

name: S5
positive_test: A simplified multi-input multi-output S4.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: H3
positive_test: An S4-based layer with shift and diagonal SSMs plus multiplicative interactions.

name: Mamba
positive_test: A selective state space model whose parameters are input-dependent.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2); the family is young relative to the snapshot.

name: Recurrent state space model (RSSM)
positive_test: A latent dynamics model with a deterministic recurrent path and a stochastic state, trained to predict observations and rewards.
negative_test: Not the planning or actor-critic procedure that uses it (-> algorithms).
notes: R5 hybrid. This is the model entity behind world-model RL papers.

name: Autoencoder
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: An encoder and a decoder trained so that the output reconstructs the input through a bottleneck; the learned object is both networks.
negative_test: Excludes an encoder-decoder trained to map between two different signals (-> the relevant backbone), and excludes U-Net, which has no bottleneck code.
notes: Root (R6), and the weakest of them: it is defined partly by what it learns, which is the rejected `function learned' characteristic. Kept because the encoder-bottleneck-decoder shape is structural and the compute profile is distinctive. See SELF_AUDIT.

name: Variational autoencoder
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: An autoencoder whose code is a learned distribution regularised to a prior and trained by a variational bound.
negative_test: Not the ELBO/reparameterisation procedure alone.
notes: Boundary case: also a deep directed latent-variable model; only the autoencoder edge is asserted, from the paper's own title.

name: beta-VAE
positive_test: A VAE with an up-weighted KL term for disentanglement.
notes: Differs from parent by: objective weighting.

name: Conditional VAE
positive_test: A VAE whose encoder and decoder condition on a label or context.

name: VQ-VAE
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A VAE with a discrete codebook latent.
examples: vq-vae; vqvae-2; discrete variational autoencoder; dynamic vector quantization

name: VQGAN
positive_test: A VQ-VAE trained with an adversarial and perceptual loss.
notes: R5 hybrid.

name: Denoising autoencoder
positive_test: An autoencoder trained to reconstruct a clean input from a corrupted one.
negative_test: Not a diffusion denoiser, which is a U-Net inside a diffusion system.

name: Sparse autoencoder
positive_test: An autoencoder with an overcomplete, sparsity-penalised code.
notes: Possibly speculative under this name (phase 2); the interpretability usage post-dates the snapshot.

name: MADE
positive_test: An autoencoder with masked connections giving an autoregressive factorisation.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Generative adversarial network
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A generator network paired with a discriminator that scores its samples; the learned object is both networks.
negative_test: Excludes objective-only variants whose architecture is unchanged (WGAN, LSGAN) -- those are algorithms, as SimCLR is.
notes: Root (R6).

name: DCGAN
positive_test: A GAN with a strided-convolutional generator and discriminator.
notes: R5 hybrid. Possibly speculative under this name (phase 2).

name: Progressive GAN
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A GAN grown progressively in resolution during training.
notes: Possibly speculative under this name (phase 2).

name: StyleGAN
positive_test: A style-based generator with a mapping network and AdaIN modulation.
notes: R1: built on the ProGAN generator. Generations attach here.

name: Conditional GAN
positive_test: A GAN whose generator and discriminator both condition on a label or input.

name: Pix2Pix
positive_test: A conditional GAN for paired image-to-image translation.

name: CycleGAN
positive_test: Two generators and two discriminators wired in a cycle for unpaired translation.
negative_test: Boundary: the cycle-consistency loss alone would make it an algorithm; the two-generator wiring is what admits it as a model.
notes: See BOUNDARY_CASES: CycleGAN is admitted, WGAN is not, and the line between them is the wiring.

name: BigGAN
positive_test: A large class-conditional GAN with truncation sampling.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: SRGAN
positive_test: A GAN for single-image super-resolution.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Normalizing flow
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: An invertible network with a tractable Jacobian determinant, so densities transform exactly in both directions.
negative_test: Excludes GFlowNets, which are not invertible maps and share only the word `flow'.
examples: realnvp; glow; maf; continuous normalizing flow
notes: Root (R6).

name: NICE
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: Additive coupling layers with unit Jacobian.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: RealNVP
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: Affine coupling layers with a triangular Jacobian.
notes: R1: `we extend NICE'.

name: Glow
positive_test: RealNVP with invertible 1x1 convolutions and actnorm.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Masked autoregressive flow
positive_test: A flow whose transforms are stacked MADE autoregressive conditioners.
notes: R5 hybrid. Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Inverse autoregressive flow
positive_test: An autoregressive flow parameterised for fast sampling.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Continuous normalizing flow
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A flow defined by an ODE, with the log-density change given by the trace of the Jacobian.
examples: cnf; continuous normalizing flow; categorical normalizing flows
notes: R5 hybrid.

name: FFJORD
positive_test: A CNF with a stochastic trace estimator.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Embedding model
characteristic: what the discrete entity indexed by the table is: a word type, a node of one graph, or an entity/relation of a knowledge graph
positive_test: The learned object is a table of vectors indexed by discrete entities, scored by a cheap fixed function (dot product, translation, bilinear form).
negative_test: Excludes an embedding *layer* inside a larger network: the table must be the model.
notes: Root (R6), and the one I constructed rather than found: no single paper founds it. See SELF_AUDIT -- lowest-confidence root and lowest-confidence division.

name: Word embedding model
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: The indexed entity is a word or subword type, and the table is the model.
negative_test: Excludes contextual embeddings produced by a network (-> that network).
notes: R4. Possibly speculative as a whole subtree: no corpus support (phase 2), kept because the field is real and the snapshot is one year.

name: word2vec
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A log-linear predictor of context from word, or word from context, whose weight matrix is the embedding.

name: CBOW
positive_test: The continuous-bag-of-words architecture.
notes: One of the two architectures named in the word2vec paper.

name: Skip-gram
positive_test: The skip-gram architecture.
notes: The other architecture named in the word2vec paper.

name: GloVe
positive_test: Embeddings fitted to a log co-occurrence factorisation.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: fastText
positive_test: Word vectors as sums of character n-gram vectors.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Node embedding model
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: The indexed entity is a node of one fixed graph; the table does not generalise to new graphs.
negative_test: Excludes GNNs, which learn functions, not tables.

name: DeepWalk
positive_test: Skip-gram over random walks on a graph.
notes: Possibly speculative under this name (phase 2); the *2vec graph-embedding pattern is attested.

name: node2vec
positive_test: DeepWalk with biased second-order walks.

name: LINE
positive_test: Node embeddings preserving first- and second-order proximity.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Knowledge graph embedding model
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: The indexed entities are the entities and relations of a knowledge graph, scored as triples.
negative_test: Excludes text encoders applied to verbalised triples.

name: TransE
positive_test: Relations as translations in embedding space.

name: DistMult
positive_test: A diagonal bilinear triple score.

name: ComplEx
positive_test: A bilinear score in complex space, capturing asymmetry.

name: RotatE
positive_test: Relations as rotations in complex space.

name: Matrix factorization model
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A matrix approximated as a product of two learned low-rank factors.
negative_test: Not the ALS/SGD fitting procedure.
examples: matrix factorization; svd recommender; bprmf; cp decomposition

name: Non-negative matrix factorization
positive_test: Matrix factorization with non-negativity constraints.

name: Factorization machine
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: Pairwise feature interactions modelled by inner products of per-feature latent vectors.

name: DeepFM
positive_test: A factorization machine and an MLP sharing one embedding table.
notes: R5 hybrid; the anchor for the deep-recommender cluster.

name: Spiking neural network
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: Units communicating by discrete spike events with membrane-potential dynamics; the learned object is the synaptic weights (and sometimes the time constants).
negative_test: Excludes rate-coded networks trained by backpropagation with no spike dynamics.
examples: snn; spiking neural network; lif network
notes: Root (R6). Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2); kept because it is a distinct founding idea that a one-year snapshot can easily miss.

name: Spiking CNN
positive_test: A convnet whose units are spiking.
notes: R5 hybrid. Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Rule-based model
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: The learned object is an explicit set of symbolic conditions applied in order or as a set.
negative_test: Excludes decision trees, which are a separate root, and excludes rules extracted post hoc from another model (that is an explanation, not the model).
examples: decision list; rule set; corels; logic program
notes: Root (R6). Flagged in phase 1 as my most speculative root; phase 2 found CORELS/FairCORELS in the corpus, so it is attested.

name: Decision list
positive_test: An ordered list of if-then rules with a default.
notes: Attested in phase 2 via CORELS.

name: Rule set
positive_test: An unordered set of rules combined by voting or coverage.
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Logic program (ILP hypothesis)
positive_test: A learned set of first-order clauses.
examples: ilp hypothesis; prolog program; neural-symbolic rules
notes: Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2). Kept on the domains external-diff finding that logic/relational learning is a genuine blind spot.

name: 3D Gaussian splatting
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: An explicit, optimizable set of anisotropic Gaussian primitives with position, covariance, opacity and colour, rendered by differentiable rasterisation.
negative_test: Excludes coordinate MLPs: there is no network.
notes: Root (R6), and a single-artifact root, which is the exact smell R6 warns about. Kept because its framing is an explicit contrast with NeRF (reading (d)), so no ancestor exists here. Possibly speculative: no corpus support (phase 2).

name: Flow network (GFlowNet)
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A network parameterising edge or state flows over a DAG of construction actions, so that completed objects are sampled in proportion to a reward.
negative_test: Not the training objective (trajectory balance, detailed balance, flow matching) -- that is an algorithm -- and not a normalizing flow, which is an invertible density map.
examples: gflownet; generative flow network; dyngfn; continuous gflownet
notes: Added in phase 2 as a NEW ROOT: the largest blind spot of the draft, and a failure of my own recall rather than of the field. R6 applied to it makes it a root -- nothing in the tree is its ancestor. Flagged in SELF_AUDIT for a deeper design pass: its variant set is large.

name: Neural operator
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A model learning a mapping between function spaces, discretisation-invariant by construction; the learned object is the kernel-integral parameters.
negative_test: Excludes a convnet trained on PDE solutions at a fixed grid resolution.
examples: fourier neural operator; fno; graph neural operator; deeponet
notes: Added in phase 2 (blind spot). Root by R6: the graph-neural-operator framing would give a GNN parent, but FNO's own framing is operator-first.

name: Fourier neural operator
positive_test: A neural operator parameterising the kernel integral directly in Fourier space.
notes: Added in phase 2.

name: Slot attention
characteristic: (descent -- children are lineage descendants, R1; no dividing principle)
positive_test: A fixed set of permutation-symmetric slots competing for input features through attention normalised over slots, refined by a recurrent update.
negative_test: Excludes ordinary cross-attention, where the softmax is over keys and queries do not compete.
examples: slot attention; dinosaur; bo-qsa; disentangled slot attention
notes: Added in phase 2 as a NEW ROOT (object-centric cluster). Boundary case: it defines itself against standard dot-product attention, which argues for a Transformer parent, but the competition and the recurrent update are not modifications of the Transformer block, and it fits none of the three stack divisions.
